name: Yakima
deadline_pattern: July 1 each year for the following calendar year
notes: Nonprofits and public agencies only; preference for city-owned tourism facilities and year-round promotion through the DMO.

presentation.pattern: City staff and the LTAC review written applications after the July 1 deadline; no applicant presentation is mentioned

funding_docs.title: Tourism Promotion Grants (Lodging Tax funded) program page
funding_docs.summary: Applications accepted June 1 to July 1, 2026 for 2027 grants; limited to nonprofits and public agencies, with preference for city-owned facilities generating overnight stays and year-round promotion through the DMO. No dollar total is published.

funding_docs.title: FY 2027 Lodging Tax Grant Funds application
funding_docs.summary: Official 2027 application form (Word); requires a contract with the City and a final report. Amount available not stated.

funding_docs.title: City of Yakima Opens 2027 Tourism Promotion Grant Applications
funding_docs.summary: June 4, 2026 news release: applications due July 1, 2026; LTAC and staff review, Council makes final awards.

pool_note: No lodging tax revenue, grant pool or award list is published on the city's grant pages; 2027 applications closed July 1, 2026.

name: Wenatchee
deadline_pattern: Rolling; applications due one week before each joint LTAC/TPA meeting until funds run out
notes: Event-focused reimbursement grants reviewed jointly with the Tourism Promotion Area board; 2026 LTAC budget of $100K was nearly spent by May 2026.

presentation.pattern: Applicants present to the joint LTAC/TPA meeting following their submission; applications due one week before the meeting

meeting_schedule: Joint LTAC/TPA meetings roughly monthly on a Wednesday at 12:00 pm, City Hall 2nd floor meeting room (2026: May 20, June 17; 2024: May 15, Jun 26, Jul 17, Aug 21, Sep 18)

funding_docs.title: Tourism Promotion Area / Lodging Tax program page
funding_docs.summary: Grants fund marketing or operations of events and festivals that attract tourists; applications due one week before each joint LTAC/TPA meeting, first come first served; reimbursement with a 60-day post-event report. Lists 2024 awards such as $19,330 to Tour de Bloom and $15,000 to Apple Cup.

funding_docs.title: Joint LTAC/TPA meeting packet, June 17, 2026
funding_docs.summary: Funding tracker shows a 2026 LTAC budget of $100,000 (fully committed by May 31) and a TPA budget of $45,000 with $25,361 remaining; includes pending requests from Pybus Market ($3,510) and the YMCA ($25,000) and recent awards of $10,000 to Wenatchee Youth Baseball and $6,000 to La Terraza.

pool_note: 2026: the LTAC grant budget was $100,000 (fully committed by May 31) plus a separate $45,000 TPA budget; total lodging tax revenue and standing commitments are not in the packet, so the competitive figure is the grant budget only.

name: Leavenworth
deadline_pattern: Summer each year (August 10 in 2026; June 10 in 2024) for the following calendar year
contact: Courtney Porter (2027 cycle); Sue Cragun, Executive Assistant, (509) 668-9077
notes: Run as the Leavenworth Fund Lodging Tax Fund; 501(c) nonprofits or fiscally sponsored groups only, max $10K for events and $5K for secondary attractions, reimbursement basis.

presentation.pattern: City Council Economic Development Committee reviews written applications and forwards recommendations to Council; no presentation mentioned

funding_docs.title: Leavenworth Fund Grant Program 2027 Overview and Guidelines
funding_docs.summary: $150,000 Lodging Tax Fund; caps of $10,000 for Primary Draw events and festivals and $5,000 for Secondary Attractions; 501(c) nonprofits only; priority when the grant is 50% or less of project cost.

funding_docs.title: Which Fund? Leavenworth Fund Grant Program 2027
funding_docs.summary: Explains the split between the Lodging Tax Fund (tourism projects inside the lodging tax boundary, visitors from 50+ miles) and the General Fund ($5,000 cap, resident benefit); lists ineligible costs and the 50% match expectation.

funding_docs.title: The 2027 Leavenworth Fund Grant Program is now open
funding_docs.summary: Announces $150,000 Lodging Tax Fund and $75,000 General Fund for 2027 with applications due 11:59 pm August 10, 2026.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Boundary Map 2027
funding_docs.summary: Map of the area in which Lodging Tax Fund projects must take place.

pool_note: 2027: $150,000 Lodging Tax Fund grant pool for nonprofits, capped at $10,000 per event; the city's total lodging tax revenue and its share kept for other tourism uses are not published.

name: Ocean Shores
deadline_pattern: Proposals accepted September 1-30 each year per LTAC page; extra rounds when excess funds exist (e.g., March 2024)
contact: Denise Siers, LTAC Chair, dsiers@osgov.com; City Clerk, slogan@osgov.com, 360-289-2022
notes: Most of the pool goes to the Ocean Shores Convention Center ($1.1M of $1.5M in 2025), leaving a small amount for outside groups.

presentation.pattern: LTAC meets two or three times in October after the September 30 proposal deadline to review proposals before Council

meeting_schedule: Meets as necessary, no regular schedule; typically two or three meetings in October

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page
funding_docs.summary: Written proposals go to the City Clerk September 1-30; the City sets the amount available from the lodging tax pool each year; committee is five members appointed by the Mayor with Councilmember Denise Siers as chair.

funding_docs.title: Public Notice: Lodging Tax Program applications (March 2024 round)
funding_docs.summary: Excess-funds round open March 1-29, 2024; applicants must show other funding sources, community benefit, board list, schedule and past experience; projects that increase overnight stays favored.

funding_docs.title: Ocean Shores Awards $1.5M for 'heads in beds' (The Daily World)
funding_docs.summary: Council approved $1.5 million in 2025 lodging tax awards to 10 recipients on the LTAC's recommendation, with $1.1 million going to the Ocean Shores Convention Center.

pool_note: 2025: $1.5M awarded across 10 recipients, with $1.1M to the city's Ocean Shores Convention Center, leaving about $400,000 for the other nine recipients (estimate; the 2021 cycle left only about $19,000 for outside groups).

name: Long Beach
deadline_pattern: Early October each year (Oct 1-3) for the following calendar year
notes: Requires liability insurance naming the City and an economic impact report within 60 days of the event; 2027 cycle not found online.

funding_docs.title: 2026 Lodging Tax Funds application
funding_docs.summary: Application for tourism events, facilities and marketing due October 3 at 5:00 pm; eligible applicants are tourism marketing entities, 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) nonprofits and municipalities; awardees sign a services contract, carry liability insurance and file an economic impact report within 60 days. No total stated.

funding_docs.title: 2022 Lodging Tax Funds application
funding_docs.summary: Earlier version of the same form with an October 1 deadline; same eligibility categories and a 30-day economic impact report.

pool_note: No funding total, award list or budget for the lodging tax fund was found online; only the application form is posted.

name: Olympia
tax_rate: 4% special excise tax (first 2% credited against state sales tax)
deadline_pattern: Annual cycle; committee reviews applications in June/July and early October
notes: Nonprofits and government entities only; promotion must target audiences outside Thurston County; applications through Submittable, reimbursement basis.

presentation.pattern: Committee reviews applications at its June/July meeting and finalizes recommendations in early October

meeting_schedule: Usually meets three times a year, including June/July and early October

funding_docs.title: 2027 Tourism Funding Application Guidelines
funding_docs.summary: Official 2027 guidelines (PDF dated Sept 3, 2026); the LTAC page summarizes priorities as overnight stays in Olympia lodging, promotion to out-of-county visitors, economic benefit, no duplication, City-owned facilities, and applicants not relying solely on LTAC funds. Dollar total not available from the page.

funding_docs.title: LTAC Budget Workbook 2027
funding_docs.summary: Required budget workbook for 2027 applicants submitted through Submittable.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page
funding_docs.summary: Governmental entities and nonprofits may apply; reimbursement only for contracted costs; Council may approve, reject or return recommendations but cannot add recipients or change amounts.

pool_note: No pool or award total is published on the LTAC page; the 2027 guidelines PDF could not be read in this pass.

name: Lacey
deadline_pattern: Late August each year for the following calendar year; presentations mid-September
notes: Covers Lacey and its Urban Growth Area; reimbursement-only with a Professional Services Agreement; pool is the 2026 awards total.

presentation.pattern: LTAC may request a supplemental presentation from applicants about four weeks after the late-August deadline (anticipated Sept 17, 2026)

meeting_schedule: No fixed schedule; meets in September for application review (hybrid: Lacey City Hall Executive Board Room, Zoom and YouTube), with awards in January

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page with 2026 awards
funding_docs.summary: 2026 awards total about $685,239: $278,739 to the Regional Athletic Complex, $100,000 to Experience Olympia and Beyond, $80,000 to the Olympia/Lacey Fan Zone, $40,000 to Oly Soccer and $35,000 to the Lacey Visitors Center; events category totals about $191,500.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax Funding Scoring Rubric
funding_docs.summary: 160-point rubric: activity frequency (30), location inside Lacey/UGA (30), tourism promotion with 50 points for visitors from 50+ miles, and community collaboration (50).

funding_docs.title: DRAFT 2027 Lodging Tax Funding Application
funding_docs.summary: Question set for the 2027 cycle (closed August 21, 2026); reimbursement-only funding under a Professional Services Agreement.

funding_docs.title: 2025 Adopted Budget (lodging tax recipients)
funding_docs.summary: Adopted budget listing 2025 lodging tax recipients and amounts.

pool_note: 2026: $685,239 awarded in total; about $319,739 went to City of Lacey facilities and events (Regional Athletic Complex $278,739, Lacey Museum $30,000, July 3 fireworks $11,000) and $100,000 to the Experience Olympia DMO, leaving about $265,500 across 15 outside recipients (estimate).

name: Bellingham
deadline_pattern: Early September each year for the following calendar year
notes: Tiers: Visitor-Generating Events up to $100K/yr (2-year term), Destination Experience up to $35K, Small Grant up to $5K, plus Signature Event grants; LTAC is a subcommittee of the Tourism Commission.

presentation.pattern: Tourism Commission reviews proposals after the early-September deadline; no applicant presentation mentioned

meeting_schedule: Tourism Commission typically meets the fourth Tuesday of each month, Mayor's Boardroom, Bellingham City Hall

funding_docs.title: Tourism Grant Application (2027 cycle)
funding_docs.summary: Due September 4, 2026 at noon; Visitor-Generating Events up to $100,000/yr (two-year term, average about $40,000), Destination Experience up to $35,000, Small Grant up to $5,000; staff estimate about $400,000 went to events and $300,000 to destination experience projects last cycle; 100-point scoring led by economic impact and Bellingham identity.

funding_docs.title: Tourism Grant Program overview
funding_docs.summary: Describes the three grant tiers plus Signature Event grants for experienced producers; funded by the City's share of lodging tax.

funding_docs.title: Tourism Eligible Expenses and Marketing Requirements
funding_docs.summary: Lists eligible costs and the pre- and post-contract marketing meetings required with Bellingham Whatcom County Tourism.

funding_docs.title: Tourism Grant Application Budget Form
funding_docs.summary: Required project budget template for applicants.

pool_note: 2026 cycle: staff estimate about $400,000 went to Visitor-Generating Events and $300,000 to Destination Experience grants, roughly $700,000 to outside applicants (estimate); total city lodging tax revenue not published on the grant pages.

name: Mount Vernon
deadline_pattern: Early September each year for the following calendar year
notes: Applications go to the Finance Office by 4:30 pm; prior-year recipients must file a post-event report by December 31.

funding_docs.title: 2027 Lodging Tax/Tourism Promotion application packet
funding_docs.summary: 2027 application packet due to the Finance Office by 4:30 pm September 8, 2026. Amount available not stated on the page.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax information and instructions
funding_docs.summary: General program information and instructions for applicants (content not retrievable in this pass).

funding_docs.title: 2026 Post Event Report Form
funding_docs.summary: Required of 2026 recipients by December 31, 2026.

pool_note: No funding total or award list is published with the 2027 application packet.

name: Burlington
deadline_pattern: Mid-September each year for the following calendar year, with occasional second rounds (Nov 14, 2025 for 2026)
contact: Kristen Bachhuber, HR & Admin Manager, kristenb@burlingtonwa.gov, 360-755-0531
notes: Paper or emailed applications to City Hall or the Finance Department; seven voting LTAC members plus alternates.
meeting_schedule: Meets as needed at City Hall

funding_docs.title: 2026 Burlington Lodging Tax Application
funding_docs.summary: Application form for 2026 lodging tax funds for organizations that promote tourism in Burlington.

funding_docs.title: News Release: 2026 Lodging Tax Applications (second round)
funding_docs.summary: Second-round applications due 5:00 pm November 14, 2025 to City Hall or kristenb@burlingtonwa.gov.

funding_docs.title: Burlington City Council allocates lodging tax funds (goSkagit)
funding_docs.summary: Council approved $700,000 for 2026 (LTAC had recommended $650,000): about $240,000 to the Chamber/Visitor Center including Berry Dairy Days, about $147,000 to Parks tournament support at Skagit River Park, $57,000 to the Skagit Tourism Bureau sports commission and $50,000 to the Children's Museum.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee page
funding_docs.summary: Roster of the seven-member committee and link to the 2027 Lodging Tax Application Process document.

pool_note: 2026: Council allocated $700,000 (LTAC recommended $650,000); about $240,000 went to the Chamber/Visitor Information Center contract and $147,000 to city Parks tournament support, leaving roughly $313,000 for outside groups such as the Skagit Tourism Bureau ($57,000) and Children's Museum ($50,000) (estimate).
